title: The Long Way Back
subtitle: Irish whiskey, 1880 to now
description: How Irish whiskey went from the biggest whiskey trade of the 1800s to two distilleries by 1980, and how it recovered after 1987. Four pours.

pours.name: Redbreast 12 Year Old
pours.notes: Notice the texture before the flavour. Unmalted barley is usually credited with a thick, oily feel.

pours.name: Bushmills 10 Year Old
pours.notes: Malted barley only, distilled three times. Put it beside the Redbreast and compare the weight.

pours.name: Powers Gold Label
pours.notes: Pot still whiskey blended with column-still grain whiskey, the mix John's Lane once refused. Taste it after the Redbreast.

pours.name: Connemara Original Peated Single Malt
pours.notes: Peat smoke and two distillations, both unusual in Irish whiskey when Cooley started.
